# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.access;

/** A setting on a sheet: its key and value (null: blank), and the from-date it was saved from when one was given (null otherwise). */
public record Setting(String sheetId, String key, String value, java.time.LocalDate from) {

    /** Whether the key's setting is dated: one that carries a figure (every key but the policy date, period numbering from, the entry date, the grace days, the escalation gap, the fiscal start month, the pot, the alert threshold, the parent and the permissions). */
    public static boolean isDated(String key) {
        return !POLICY_DATE.equals(key) && !POT.equals(key) && !ALERT_THRESHOLD.equals(key) && !PARENT.equals(key) && !PERIOD_NUMBERING_FROM.equals(key) && !ENTRY_DATE.equals(key) && !GRACE_DAYS.equals(key) && !ESCALATE_AFTER.equals(key) && !FISCAL_START_MONTH.equals(key) && !isPermission(key);
    }

    /** Whether the key is one of the permission matrix's (perm-<action>). */
    public static boolean isPermission(String key) {
        return key.startsWith(PERMISSION) && PERMISSION_STANDING.containsKey(key.substring(PERMISSION.length()));
    }

    /** The value a dated key has before every from-date: the floor's, the terms' and the late percent's starting value; null (blank) for the rest. */
    public static String starting(String key) {
        return switch (key) {
            case FLOOR -> FLOOR_DEFAULT;
            case TERMS -> TERMS_DEFAULT;
            case LATE_PCT -> LATE_PCT_DEFAULT;
            default -> null;
        };
    }

    /** The most a clerk may settle a claim's due for; blank means no limit. */
    public static final String CLERK_LIMIT = "clerk-limit";

    /** The due above which a claim needs a proof before it is settled or approved; blank means none. */
    public static final String PROOF_THRESHOLD = "proof-threshold";

content.text:
The review SLA is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

- **Setting:** `review-sla` is a new setting that isn't dated. It takes a whole number of days, and blank means none. Saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED key=review-sla value=<days>` to the audit file, with an empty value when blank. It's in the settings form next to the escalation setting.
- **Review day:** I didn't add a new column. A claim's status log already records the date of each status change, so for a claim in REVIEW the server sends the date of its last REVIEW line. That date is the sheet's today when it went to REVIEW. Claims in any other status get no review day. The log lookup is in `ClaimLogRepository.java`, and the claims list sends the date in `RespondWithClaims.java`.
- **Screen:** a new file, `features/reviewsla/reviewSla.slot.tsx`, shows `claim-review-late` as `yes` when all three hold:
  - the claim is in REVIEW;
  - the SLA is set;
  - the review day plus the SLA days is before the sheet's today.

  Otherwise it shows `no`. The summary panel has a new `summary-review-late-count` that counts the claims marked `yes`.
